resources.string: Import a subscription, a share link, or scan a QR code from the Profiles tab.
"Connected" is shown only after a real request has passed through the tunnel and come back.
Connect to see the live speed here — this area answers “how fast is it right now?”
What carries your traffic — a protocol core, or none for a plain VPN. Freely combinable with any network below, exactly like Aether.
Only the tunnel — no protocol core. The network choice below is the whole connection.
The Psiphon network (bundled core) — rotating transports built for filtered networks. Slower than WARP, much harder to block. Exclusive: on failure you get the real error, never a silent WARP swap.
The real Tor network (bundled tor 0.4.8, obfs4 + webtunnel bridges). Slowest option, strongest censorship resistance. Exclusive: on failure you get the real error, never a silent WARP swap.
How the connection reaches the internet — independent of the protocol. Direct is Aether\'s architecture: the core connects straight from your ISP, no WARP in the middle.
Straight from your ISP — Aether\'s own architecture and the proven fastest path. Only offered together with a protocol.
With a protocol: direct first, then the WARP-chained path as a safety net. Plain VPN: the auto-ranked WARP chain (MASQUE TCP-443 → UDP-443 → WireGuard).
WARP over MASQUE (the TCP-443 + UDP-443 wires race). With a protocol: the chain rides ONLY the MASQUE engine.
Plain WireGuard straight to Cloudflare (UDP). With a protocol: the chain rides ONLY the WireGuard sidecar — an ISP reset fails honestly.
Two WARP tunnels chained — the second hop rides inside the first. Plain VPN only. Experimental.
How hard and how long the engine hunts for a working endpoint before handing over.
Shortest sweep — connect fast or move on.
The default. Good on most networks.
Patient sweep across every endpoint — for networks where edges are slow.
No UDP at all: only MASQUE over plain TCP 443, indistinguishable from ordinary HTTPS.
The longest, most persistent sweep — every transport, every endpoint.
Takes effect on the next connect.
Which country the Psiphon exit should be in. Auto lets the network pick the fastest server; a fixed country is slower to find but always egresses there.
Bridges hide tor from the censor. The auto list is refreshed on every app build.
A fresh bridge list is baked into the app at build time — no setup needed.
Paste your own Bridge lines (obfs4/webtunnel from bridges.torproject.org or a trusted sender).
Plain tor without bridges — only for networks where tor is not filtered at all.
obfs4 1.2.3.4:443 CERT… cert=… iat-mode=0\nwebtunnel [2001:db8…]:443 FP… url=https://… ver=0.0.4
Connected — but through the WARP fallback: %1$s failed first (%2$s). Disconnect and retry, or check the Logs page for details.
Kuku itself is always excluded from the tunnel to avoid a routing loop.
If the tunnel dies unexpectedly, the VPN interface stays up so no traffic leaks outside the tunnel. Enable the system "Always-on VPN + Block without VPN" for the strongest protection.
If the selected profile cannot prove a real connection, ranked alternatives are tried and the successful one is remembered.
Iranian sites & apps bypass the tunnel

Banking, government and other Iranian domains/IPs connect directly (no tunnel tax, no foreign exit IP for domestic services); everything else rides the tunnel. The list is the community geosite/geoip “ir” category.
Drops connections to known ad and tracker domains (community ads-all list) inside the tunnel — apps see fewer ads without any per-app setup.
If the lists cannot be downloaded on your network, the tunnel still connects — just without that rule.

For heavy-filtering days: one switch and every connect tries the FULL ranked chain for your chosen protocol — direct first, then every underlay — with the most patient sweep. No re-pinning needed. Turn it off when things calm down.

Full-device VPN: ALL phone traffic goes through the tunnel. Switch it off to run a local proxy only — then apps that support SOCKS/HTTP (browsers, Telegram…) can use 127.0.0.1:2080 while nothing else is touched.
Local proxy only: the phone’s traffic is NOT routed automatically; only apps you point at 127.0.0.1:2080 (SOCKS/HTTP) use the tunnel. Switch it on for a full-device VPN.
Share the proxy on the local network

While connected, other devices on the phone’s hotspot/Wi-Fi can ride this tunnel by setting their proxy to the phone’s IP on port %1$d (SOCKS/HTTP). Only enable on a network you trust — this proxy has no password.
All profiles and settings in one JSON file — export before reinstalling, restore on a new phone. The file never leaves the device unless you share it.
You are on the latest version
New version available: %1$s — tap to open the release page

1.7.4 — (1) Tor flag, take two: the country lookup now asks about the KNOWN exit IP and leads with geojs.io (no Cloudflare in front — the classic Tor-user geo answer), then ip-api.com (plain HTTP) and ipinfo.io for the SAME IP; when every web source still refuses, the flag falls back to what the Psiphon core itself reported about its exit region. (2) AI mode: a dedicated section for the AI services — the bundled Psiphon core with a HARD US egress (EgressRegion=US), one tap on Home, the US flag on the tile tells you it worked; the regular Psiphon candidates stay behind it as the safety net. (3) Speed test moved to Profiles (Home\'s button was the wrong home): every profile row has its own test icon — the app connects THAT profile, measures real down/up/ping and announces the verdict weak / medium / good / excellent next to the chart. (4) Add-profile dialog fixed: it scrolls now, survives the keyboard, shows how many config links the paste contains, and imports multiple configs at once — the Profiles section is completed, not removed

1.7.3 — two field fixes from your logs. (1) Psiphon over WireGuard: the sidecar\'s liveness probe used a HOSTNAME, so every check first had to push a DoH query (TLS-inside-WireGuard) through the young tunnel — on your ISP that extra handshake stalled past the 8s cap and ALL ten endpoint attempts looked dead (the ten × 8s "lookup failed for www.cloudflare.com" in your log) while the wire itself was never the suspect. The probe now dials the IP literal 1.1.1.1 directly (zero DNS), DNS inside the underlay is one plain UDP query through the encrypted tunnel instead of TLS-in-TLS, the first cold attempt gets a 12s window — and if the WG wire still refuses, the chain now falls through to standalone Psiphon instead of dying with "all 1 candidate(s) failed". (2) Tor flag: every country source was Cloudflare-hosted or -fronted, so an exit that was challenged once was challenged again and the flag never came; the resolver now walks ipwho.is → ip-api.com (plain HTTP, no Cloudflare) → ipinfo.io until one answers the country

1.7.2 — flag + IP together in every mode: the exit tile is double-width so the flag and the full address both fit, exit info resolves in the background right after connect, and when an exit refuses Cloudflare\'s trace (Tor does), the app now also asks the Tor Project\'s own IP API and ipwho.is for the country. Real speed test on Home: one tap measures the ACTUAL download/upload/ping of the connected method through the tunnel — WARP, gool, Kuku→Psiphon and Kuku→Tor are all measured the same way, so «which method is best» becomes a number. Auto-reconnect on Wi-Fi/data switch: the session bounces to the new network and the per-network wiring memory leads with the method that worked there — the best method picks itself. Psiphon over WireGuard: the WG underlay now sweeps the same anycast endpoint pool as the plain WARP path — an ISP that blocks only some 162.159.x IPs no longer kills the wire (what the Aether comparison showed)

1.7.1 — three fixes. (1) The Exit-IP tile showed broken text like [C@fbd365e instead of the address: the new country-flag code joined raw char arrays; the flag now renders properly beside a real IP, on the Home tile and in the notification. (2) Psiphon/Tor stopped connecting after the good 1.6.9: the new Iranian-bypass rule-set downloads ran ON the connect path, so every candidate sat up to ~80s behind blocked-CDN timeouts before its core even booted. Downloads now happen through the live tunnel right after a verified connect and connects read only cached files — the connect path is as fast as 1.6.9 again. (3) The Home screen scrolled a little; it now fits the phone screen exactly with no scrolling — a slightly more compact chart and button

1.7.0 — country flag next to the exit IP, a redesigned self-explanatory speed chart, the VPN/proxy switch moved to Settings with a real explanation, a Quick Settings tile for one-tap connect, live speed in the notification, Iranian sites/apps bypass (banking apps stay direct), a system-wide ad blocker, selectable encrypted DNS, an emergency mode, proxy sharing over the local network, and backup/restore of everything

Source code, issues and new releases
1.4.1 — About page: version, engine and GitHub link

1.6.9 — The bridge decay, finished. Root cause: the bridge collector stopped updating in July, and only ~11% of the bundled bridge lines still accept a TCP connection — tor was cycling corpses. Now every bridge is TCP-tested on the device before the boot (dead ones dropped, counted in the log); if too few survive, FRESH bridges (official BridgeDB distribution + collector) are fetched through WARP and put first; a stalled bootstrap retries once on a different bridge set; CI ships only bridges that passed the same TCP test

1.6.8 — Your field log, answered with three fixes. (1) Wiring memory: the path that last VERIFIED on this network (direct, or Kuku→core over MASQUE/WireGuard) now leads every Psiphon/Tor connect — the dead direct attempt (75s) and the dead WireGuard underlay (~30s) are paid ONCE, not on every connect. (2) Tor stops burning the full 4-minute cap: a bootstrap with no new progress for 2 minutes fails fast with its last %, so the chain reaches the Kuku→Tor underlay that actually works on your ISP. (3) The snowflake transport (v2.5.1) is bundled with the two built-in bridge lines — the domain-fronted transport that survives where IP-based obfs4/webtunnel bridges get swept; Bridge mode auto now ships obfs4 + webtunnel + snowflake

1.6.7 — The Aether split, exactly as you drew it: the Connection page now has two independent selectors — پروتکل (Protocol: none / Psiphon / Tor) and شبکه (Network: Direct / Smart / WARP-MASQUE / WARP-WireGuard). Psiphon and Tor try DIRECT first — straight from your ISP, Aether\'s own architecture and your proven fast path — instead of burning minutes on the WARP-chained path whose WireGuard underlay your ISP resets and whose MASQUE underlay leaves the core silent. A silent Psiphon core (no network notices in 75s) now fails fast instead of stalling for the full 4-minute cap. The old single method list and the underlay-wire selector are gone; old picks migrate automatically

1.6.6 — Fixed the WireGuard-underlay instant death your 1.6.5 log exposed: the sidecar engine was usually the session\'s first libbox user and its cache file landed on the read-only root (\"initialize cache-file: open cache.db: read-only file system\") — the environment setup the main core always did now also runs before the sidecar (sandbox-proven both ways on the real libbox). WireGuard-only mode no longer silently switches wires on failure, and a warm MASQUE engine with a dead egress is probed with a real request and failed honestly in seconds instead of stalling the boot for minutes

1.6.5 — The two-part split you drew from Aether: the chained modes (Kuku → Psiphon / Kuku → Tor) now ride a REAL WireGuard underlay by default (a second TUN-less engine over your registered WARP WireGuard identity — the wire Aether uses), with the MASQUE engine as fallback, and a new Underlay-wire selector on the Connection page (Auto / WireGuard only / MASQUE only)

1.6.4 — Psiphon now tries the WARP-chained path first (the same architecture you proved works on your ISP via Aether), a failing exit country automatically retries once with auto exit, and boot ticks show live progress: API reached · server list · session opening · exit region

1.6.3 — Fixed the Psiphon instant death: the core tried to create its data directory in a read-only place on Android and died before any connection — the 1.6.2 diagnostics exposed the cause; the core now uses the app\'s private storage properly, and you get a clear error if device storage is not writable
1.6.2 — Psiphon crash diagnosis: the core\'s real output is now shown on failure, stale leftover processes are killed before start, and a clean-data-store retry runs automatically

1.6.1 — No more automatic WARP fallback: when Psiphon or Tor fails (pinned on the Connection page or picked in Profiles), Kuku shows the real error and stays offline instead of quietly connecting through WARP
1.6.0 — Real Psiphon (all architectures, exit country picker) and real Tor (fresh obfs4/webtunnel bridges, own-bridge paste) — and the end of silent fallback: a WARP rescue is announced honestly
1.5.0 — Psiphon and Kuku → Psiphon: two new serverless methods
1.4.0 — FLUX turbo: live multi-path rotation, always on the fastest edge
1.3.0 — Connection page: method selector, scan modes and WARP×2 (gool)
